newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank of Italy's Visco named OECD chief economist.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy's Visco named OECD chief economist.

text.p: The Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) has named Italian central bank economist Ignazio Visco as OECD chief economist.

Visco, 47, starts his new job on August 1. He replaces Japan's Kumiharu Shigehara, who was recently appointed OECD deputy secretary general. Britain's Stephen Potter has been acting chief economist after Shigehara's change of post.
The OECD promotes free-market policy and has 29 member countries.
Visco started his career at the Bank of Italy in 1972 and has headed the Bank of Italy research department since 1990, the OECD said in a statement.
He obtained an economics degree from the University of Rome in 1971 and a doctorate in economics from the University of Pennsylvania in 1981.

He was visiting scholar at the Stanford Research Institute in Washington in 1978 and has been visiting professor of both econometrics and economic policy at the University of Rome, the statement added.
